question: A 42-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with 2 weeks of abdominal pain. She says that the pain is squeezing in character and gets worse after she eats food. The pain is particularly bad after she eats dairy products so she has begun to avoid ice cream and cheese. Furthermore, she has noticed that she has been experiencing episodes of nausea associated with abdominal pain in the last 4 days. Physical exam reveals tenderness to palpation and rebound tenderness in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. The molecule that is most likely responsible for the increased pain this patient experiences after eating fatty foods is most likely secreted by which of the following cells?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Abdominal pain after eating fatty foods" -> "Avoidance of ice cream and cheese" -> "Possible lactose intolerance" -> 70% CHAIN: "Abdominal pain in right upper quadrant" -> "Tenderness to palpation and rebound tenderness" -> "Possible cholecystitis" -> 80% CHAIN: "Abdominal pain after eating fatty foods" -> "Increased pain due to fatty foods" -> "Likely gallbladder involvement" -> 85% CHAIN: "Abdominal pain after eating fatty foods" -> "Increased pain due to fatty foods" -> "Secretion of cholecystokinin (CCK)" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The molecule most likely responsible for the increased pain this patient experiences after eating fatty foods is likely secreted by I cells, which release cholecystokinin (CCK). This hormone is involved in gallbladder contraction and the release of bile into the small intestine to aid in fat digestion. The patient's symptoms, including abdominal pain after fatty food intake and possible cholecystitis, support the role of CCK in this context.
analysis: The patient's symptoms of abdominal pain after fatty food intake, along with tenderness in the right upper quadrant, suggest a possible gallbladder issue. The molecule responsible for increased pain after eating fatty foods is likely secreted by I cells, which release cholecystokinin (CCK) to aid in fat digestion. CCK causes gallbladder contraction and bile release. Therefore, the most likely correct option is opc. I cells.
